overview: droid-use is a lightweight Android appbundle that provides a local interface for managing ADB and Shizuku shell connections without requiring a PC. It helps developers and power users streamline device debugging and script deployment by offering direct control over shell access and helper utilities directly on the device.
usecases: Re-establishing Shizuku service connections after a reboot without connecting to a computer
Deploying custom bash scripts to the local ADB shell for automated testing
Verifying current shell permissions and user context before executing sensitive system commands
howto: Install the provided .aab file using a compatible installer like SAI or via sideloading tools
Launch the app and grant necessary accessibility or system permissions to enable Shizuku or ADB mode
Use the built-in interface to check connection status, reconnect services, or paste and execute helper scripts

faq.q: Does this tool require a computer to function?
faq.a: No, it runs entirely locally on the device, though initial setup of Shizuku or ADB over Wi-Fi might require a PC for the first time.

faq.q: Is this tool safe for stable daily drivers?
faq.a: It only grants shell access that you already have; however, executing arbitrary scripts can modify system files, so proceed with caution.
